constraint_decided_it: The E11 Modification and E12 Production scope notes both say an event 'should ALSO be documented using an instance of E81 Transformation if it results in the destruction of one or more objects and the simultaneous production of others using parts or material from the originals. In this case, the new items have separate identities.' E81 and E12 are complementary, not alternatives. A quotes that sentence but glosses it as 'E81 applies instead of mere Modification' and rejects the E11 branch outright, so it omits the E12/P108 half of the pattern. B supplies it, matching the ratified examples voted in t1396 ('The transformation of the Venetian Loggia in Heraklion into a city hall (E81, E12) resulted in the City Hall of Heraklion (E24) [AND: P108 has produced the City Hall of Heraklion (E22)]'), which is the CRM's own worked case for a transformed building.
better_modelling: B substantially reached it: Hollow Farm barn (E24) <-P124 transformed- [1938 event, dual-instantiated E81 Transformation + E12 Production] -P123 resulted in-> Combe Farm barn (E24), with the same event -P108 has produced-> the Combe Farm barn; the tithe survey (E31) -P70 documents-> the Hollow Farm instance only. E22 vs E24 for the barn is not decisive: the ratified example types the same building E24 under P123 and E22 under P108. Neither answer noted that E24's threshold clause reads 'a new, distinct identity AND intended function' while the barn's function (threshing barn) is unchanged, so the identity break rests on the destructive re-erection and fabric replacement, not on function.
reasoning: Both land on the same core structure and both are within domain/range: P123 and P124 are E81 -> E18, and E24 and E22 are both E18 subclasses. A is suboptimal because it reads E11's 'should also be documented' as 'instead', rejects the modification branch, and thereby omits the more specific and ratified E12/P108 construct; it also truncates E24's 'new, distinct identity and intended function' at 'identity'. B's t1396 and t1411 citations verify verbatim, but its two t0821 quotations are silently normalised (source reads 'regardles how much simiarity', and the scare quotes around "moving"/"reconstruction"/"resurrection" are dropped), where A reproduced the typos exactly; that is a fidelity defect, not a fabrication, since t0821 msg [12] does say what B claims. Both correctly flag t0821 as Doerr's unratified proposal, though neither noticed that msg [10] (Stead) states the SIG's standing position was the opposite - buildings are treated as movable - which is what leaves E9 Move formally available for B's E22 typing.
